records.name: Johanna
records.facts_used: Johanna: The name belongs to the Johannes/Johanna family. Its Hebrew base Yohanan expresses God has been gracious. Feminine forms and renderings in different languages developed at different times; shared ancestry does not give them an identical local history. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Johanna: 1690. Its calendar year is 1901. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p181 exact feminineJohannes and own 1690/calendar 1901; neither calendar nor attestation transferred to Joanna.

records.name: Hannelora

records.name: Kristijona
records.facts_used: Kristijona: The Lithuanian form belongs to the Christianus family. Latin Christianus means a Christian and derives from Christus; Greek Christos means anointed. The historical basis of the name does not itself determine a modern bearer’s faith. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Kristijona (Kristė, Jonė) on 15 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original SalysPDF318/printed p. 303 December15femaleKristijona;PDF p. 243/printed p. 228 explicit PNChristiane. Christianus versus Christos stages distinguished.
